name: Piazza d'Italia
key_features: Postmodern plaza with a fountain shaped like Italy, curved colonnades and stainless-steel and neon details.

name: Sapporo Dome
key_features: A natural grass pitch hovers on air cushions and slides out through the wall to grow outdoors.

name: Svalbard Global Seed Vault
key_features: A wedge-shaped portal leads into a tunnel cut deep into permafrost rock, which keeps the vaults cold.

name: Toyo Ito Museum of Architecture
key_features: Polyhedral steel hut and a rebuilt light-vaulted house sit on a slope above the Seto Inland Sea.

name: Adziogol Lighthouse
key_features: Hyperboloid lattice of straight steel bars forms a light, stiff tapering tower.

name: Art Institute of Chicago, Modern Wing
key_features: A floating 'flying carpet' of aluminium blades filters north light into the top-floor galleries.

name: Asian Games Village
key_features: Clustered low-rise houses linked by narrow pedestrian lanes and gateways, recalling old Indian towns.

name: Aula Magna, Central University of Venezuela
key_features: Calder's coloured acoustic panels float below the ceiling of the fan-shaped hall to tune its sound.

name: Bankinter Building
key_features: A sharp-edged brick office block rises behind a preserved 19th-century mansion, with deep-set windows.

name: Baron Empain Palace
key_features: Reinforced-concrete mansion modelled on Hindu temples, richly decorated with animal motifs and statues.

name: Bellevue Theatre
key_features: Seaside theatre with a roof that slides open over the auditorium in summer.

name: Busan Cinema Center
key_features: Huge cantilevered roof with an LED underside shelters an outdoor theatre, carried on one cone.

name: Buzludzha Monument
key_features: Saucer-shaped concrete hall and a tall star tower on a mountain peak, now a stabilised ruin.

name: Calouste Gulbenkian Museum
by: Ruy Athouguia, Pedro Cid, Alberto Pessoa
key_features: Low concrete buildings set into a garden, opening to it through framed views.

name: Casa Planells
key_features: A narrow corner block on the Diagonal whose curved facade and wavy balconies turn the corner.

name: Centraal Beheer
key_features: Grid of concrete-block office islands linked by bridges across top-lit voids, left for users to fit out.

name: Chichu Art Museum
key_features: Galleries buried in a hill and lit only by daylight from above, each shaped around one artist.

name: Chiswick House
key_features: A neo-Palladian villa with a six-column Corinthian portico and a steep-pitched dome.

name: Cleo Rogers Memorial Library
key_features: Red brick with concrete details around Library Plaza, which holds Henry Moore's sculpture Large Arch.

name: Siida
key_features: Home to the Sámi Museum and Northern Lapland Nature Centre, on Lake Inari; opened in 1998.

name: Graduate House, University of Toronto
key_features: A dormitory block whose lettered beam cantilevers over the street as a gateway to the campus.

name: Teletón Children's Rehabilitation Centre
key_features: Prefabricated triangular panels of brick lattice fold into screens and spans that filter light.

name: Villa Gans
key_features: A protected grand residence above Kronberg im Taunus, by Peter Behrens with Camillo Karl Schneider.

name: Arts Tower
key_features: Called the most elegant university tower block of its period; 38-car paternoster lift, UK's largest surviving.

name: Bait ur Rouf Mosque
key_features: A brick cylinder inside a square, lit by skylights and perforated brick walls instead of a dome.

name: BT Tower
key_features: Cylindrical tower on a slim concrete core, its upper levels built for microwave antennas.

name: Spanish Cultural Heritage Institute ("Corona de Espinas")
key_features: Ring of stacked concrete terraces around a round courtyard, crowned by spiky fins: the "Crown of Thorns".

name: Deichman Bjørvika (Oslo Public Library)
key_features: Glass-skinned library whose upper floors cantilever out toward the Opera, with an open, see-through ground floor.

name: Delta Shelter
key_features: Steel-clad cabin on four steel columns above a flood plain; four 10 by 18 ft steel shutters roll across to close it up.

name: Diar es Saâda
key_features: Load-bearing cut-stone housing blocks stepped down a hillside around public squares.

name: Edificio Basurto
key_features: Streamline apartment tower in Condesa with rounded balconies and a celebrated snail-shell spiral stair.

name: Queen Alia International Airport
key_features: A roof of 127 shallow concrete domes on columns, inspired by Bedouin tents, shades the terminal.

name: Aiwan-e-Sadr (Presidential Palace)
key_features: Modern step-pyramid form with four main halls set in Mughal-style gardens; large rooftop solar system.

name: Bloco das Águas Livres
by: Nuno Teotónio Pereira and Bartolomeu Costa Cabral
key_features: Housing block with roof studios under half-vaults for north light, and integrated art incl. Almada Negreiros.

name: New World Center
key_features: Glass front reveals sculptural rehearsal rooms; a projection wall plays concerts to the park.

name: Borujerdi House
key_features: Courtyard house whose domed reception hall is cooled by tall windcatchers pulling air into the rooms.

name: CapitaSpring
key_features: Tower of vertical fins that part at mid-height around a spiralling open-air garden.

name: Frederic C. Hamilton Building, Denver Art Museum
by: Studio Daniel Libeskind with Davis Partnership
key_features: Titanium-clad shards lean and cantilever over the street, inspired by the Rocky Mountains' peaks.

name: Deutsches Architekturmuseum (DAM)
key_features: A 19th-century villa gutted and rebuilt inside as a 'house within a house': a gridded white shell rising through it.

name: Fukuoka Art Museum
key_features: Brick-red fired tiles cast into the concrete walls give a weathering skin facing Ohori Park.

name: Hohenhof
key_features: A total work of art: house, garden, furniture and fittings designed together for Karl Ernst Osthaus.

name: Kew House
key_features: 18 m by 9 m glass box inside rusted metal screens, cantilevered 5.5 m over a steep slope.

name: Olympic Sculpture Park
key_features: Free park with indoor pavilion and a shoreline slope built with 50,000 tonnes of riprap.

name: Tel Aviv City Hall
key_features: A concrete slab block whose upper floors project outward over the large civic square.

name: Unidad Vecinal Portales
key_features: Housing blocks linked by elevated walkways and bridges over shared gardens.

name: Usera Public Library (José Hierro)
key_features: Compact square tower of reading floors in grey cladding, with large framed windows looking over the park.

name: RIBA Headquarters (66 Portland Place)
key_features: Art Deco elements show in the bronze doors, architectural motifs and the trans-storey main window.

name: Academy of Arts, Hanseatenweg
key_features: Linked exhibition halls, studio block and a hall under a sweeping copper roof sit low in a park.

name: Asahi Group Oyamazaki Villa Museum of Art
key_features: A buried concrete cylinder gallery is reached by a stair from an older English-style hillside villa.

name: Aula Magna
key_features: Fan-shaped auditorium in brick and timber, set into the campus slope.

name: Bode Museum
key_features: A neo-baroque museum on the tip of Museum Island, its domed entrance rising straight from the river.

name: Burkina Institute of Technology
key_features: Long classroom blocks of cast earth walls under a raised metal roof that lets heat escape.

name: Church of the Autostrada del Sole
key_features: Tent-like copper roof on a forest of branching concrete supports and stone walls.

name: Churchill Gardens Estate
key_features: Nine-to-eleven storey slabs among seven-storey blocks; glass-faced accumulator tower for district heating.

name: City of Arts and Sciences
key_features: White concrete and steel ribbed buildings lined up along a former riverbed with pools.

name: Des Moines Art Center
by: Eliel Saarinen, I. M. Pei and Richard Meier
key_features: Saarinen's low stone wings around a court gain a Pei sculpture wing and a white Meier pavilion.

name: Design Museum
key_features: Restored hyperbolic paraboloid copper roof over a new oak-lined atrium.

name: Beitou Public Library
key_features: A timber library with deep balconies, a green roof and rainwater collection, set in a hot-spring park.

name: Bevin Court
by: Berthold Lubetkin (Tecton); completed with Francis Skinner and Douglas Carr Bailey
key_features: Housing block with a constructivist staircase as its social centre and prefabricated floor and wall parts.

name: Muryangsujeon, Buseoksa
key_features: One of Korea's oldest timber halls: swelling entasis columns under a hipped-and-gabled roof facing the valley.

name: Castello di Rivoli
key_features: Unfinished baroque castle turned museum, with new steel and glass insertions left distinct.

name: Hotel Humboldt
key_features: Cylindrical tower on top of the Ávila mountain ridge, reached by cable car.

name: House of the Black Madonna
key_features: Cubist facade of crystalline window frames and a faceted mansard, keeping a baroque Madonna at the corner.

name: Iate Tênis Clube, Pampulha
key_features: Lakeside club under an inverted 'butterfly' roof, raised on pilotis, one of Niemeyer's four Pampulha buildings.

name: Nagoya City Art Museum
key_features: Kept below the height of the park's trees; galleries lie underground, lit by a sunken garden.

name: OCBC Centre
key_features: Concrete slab tower whose office floors hang in stacked blocks between two half-cylinder cores.

name: Palais de Tokyo
by: André Aubert, Marcel Dastugue, Paul Viard
key_features: 1937 Art Deco palace for modern art; Lacaton & Vassal overhauled and expanded it in 2012.

name: parc de la Villette
key_features: A grid of red follies overlaid with lines of covered walks and a winding cinematic garden path.

name: Paul Löbe House
key_features: Parliament offices on the 'Band des Bundes': a glass end hall under a thin flat roof, bridged across the Spree.

name: Tempodrom
key_features: A pointed concrete tent roof recalls the circus tent the venue began in.

name: Acropolis and Philopappou Hill Paths
key_features: Paths paved with reused marble and stone fragments in irregular patterns, framing views of the Acropolis.

name: Astley Castle
key_features: New brick and timber house built inside the fire-gutted ruin; the old walls stay raw, new work sits flush in the gaps.

name: Bandung Institute of Technology (Aula Barat and Aula Timur)
key_features: Designed 1918, opened 1920; blends Indonesian vernacular architecture with modern elements.

name: BMW Headquarters (BMW Tower) and BMW Museum
key_features: Four linked cylinders like an engine, hung from a central support tower; beside it, the museum's round 'cylinder head'.

name: Bruder Klaus Field Chapel
key_features: Concrete rammed around a tent of tree trunks, then burned out to leave a charred interior.

name: Casals Hall (Ochanomizu Square)
key_features: Shoebox-style concert hall of 511 seats, with acoustic design by Nagata Acoustics.

name: Centro Cultural São Paulo
by: Eurico Prado Lopes, Luiz Benedito de Castro Telles
key_features: Horizontal reinforced-concrete and steel structure with large fluid interior spaces; opened 1982.

name: Das Gelbe Haus
key_features: Old village house stripped to its stone walls, painted white, with a new roof and one central timber column inside.

name: DZ Bank Building
key_features: A sober stone front on Pariser Platz hides a glass-roofed atrium holding a curving steel-clad conference hall.

name: Edificio López Serrano
key_features: Stepped Art Deco apartment tower in Vedado, its setback crown in the manner of New York skyscrapers.

name: National Museum of the Republic
key_features: A white concrete dome sits on the open esplanade, entered by a ramp curling out from its side.

name: Termas Geométricas
key_features: A red timber walkway threads along a forested ravine, linking a chain of hot-spring pools and huts.

name: Cedar Rock (Lowell Walter House)
key_features: Usonian tadpole plan of brick, walnut and glass; glass-walled living room faces the river; no basement or attic.

name: Hong Kong Coliseum
key_features: Indoor arena shaped like an inverted pyramid, its huge sloping bowl lifted over a glazed base.

name: Katsura Imperial Villa
key_features: Tatami-module rooms and sliding screens that inspired Taut, Gropius and Tange.

name: National Centre for the Performing Arts
key_features: Titanium and glass ellipsoid dome rising from a lake, entered through an underwater corridor.

name: One Woodward Avenue
key_features: A 28-storey International Style tower overlooking Hart Plaza and the riverfront.

name: Pennzoil Place
key_features: Two trapezoidal dark-glass towers with sloped tops nearly touch across a narrow slot.

name: St. Anna, Düren
key_features: L-shaped church whose walls are built from the rubble stone of the bombed medieval church.

name: Stazione di Venezia Santa Lucia
by: Angiolo Mazzoni, Virgilio Vallot, Paul Perilli
key_features: Low, wide rationalist station facing the Grand Canal, with Venetian lions on the flanks and 15 internal platforms.

name: Venezuela Pavilion, Venice Biennale
key_features: Small national pavilion in the Giardini designed by Carlo Scarpa in 1954-56.

name: VivoCity
key_features: Long waterfront mall with a wavy facade and a rooftop park with shallow pools.

name: Yatsushiro Municipal Museum
key_features: Galleries hidden under a grassy mound; above, light billowing roofs and a floating half-cylinder store.

name: Academy of Arts, Pariser Platz
by: Günter Behnisch with Werner Durth (Behnisch & Partner)
key_features: An all-glass front on Pariser Platz, defying the square's design rules, opening onto the old academy halls behind.

name: Alexandra Road Estate
key_features: Stepped concrete terraces line a pedestrian street, shielding the homes from the railway behind.

name: Antigone
key_features: A one-kilometre classical axis of squares and precast housing blocks running from the old town to the river Lez.

name: Aqua Tower
key_features: Slab edges vary floor to floor, so balconies form undulating contours that also shade.

name: Australia Square
key_features: Circular tower with tapering perimeter columns and a sunken public plaza at its base.

name: Azerbaijan Carpet Museum
key_features: A long building shaped like a partly rolled carpet, its metal cladding patterned like weaving.

name: Bagno Pubblico, Bellinzona
by: Aurelio Galfetti, Flora Ruchat-Roncati and Ivo Trümpy
key_features: Public pools organised along one long walkway that runs from the town to the Ticino riverbank.
